extracted.intended_audience: founders/operators of local digital news organizations, journalism entrepreneurs, and news industry professionals interested in sustainability and business operations
extracted.subtask_description: Overview of LION Publishers’ programs and standards for helping local independent online news startups develop sustainable business operations, including audits, training, funding eligibility, and operational best practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Business sustainability is the mission
rubrics_metrics.description: Every news outlet requires a sustainable business model to serve readers and advertisers and to support staff, especially new digital entrepreneurs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Journalism is the visible part of the news industry; business operations are the less visible parts. Sustainability underpins ability to do quality journalism and to retain staff; LION focuses programs around achieving business sustainability for members.

rubrics_metrics.name: Increasing revenue as the primary challenge
rubrics_metrics.description: Members report that increasing revenue is their number-one challenge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because many founders are former journalists, they often need help learning how to generate revenue; LION programming prioritizes revenue generation tactics and accountability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Set clear revenue goals
rubrics_metrics.description: News startups must set revenue goals as a core part of their planning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: LION coaching advises members to define revenue targets so budgeting, staffing, and strategy align with financial objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Create a robust budget
rubrics_metrics.description: Startups should create a robust budget that reflects realistic costs and revenue projections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Budgeting is presented as essential for sustainability; LION’s audit and educational programs help members build budgets that support staff and operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examine operational systems and processes that enable quality journalism
rubrics_metrics.description: Operate and review systems/processes (operations, workflows) that allow the organization to produce quality journalism efficiently.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Sustainability Audit and LION training ask organizations to analyze operational systems and processes; improving these systems is framed as key to both quality journalism and financial health.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sustainability Audit — complete extensive questionnaire on operational, financial, and journalism metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Members often begin with a Sustainability Audit: they complete an extensive questionnaire about operational, financial and journalism metrics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expert analysts interview members to learn more about their business ideas. Members receive an audit report with recommendations to create a more sustainable business. The Audit is often the entry point for many LION members.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sustainability Audit — interview and tailored recommendations
rubrics_metrics.description: The Audit includes analyst interviews and produces a report with recommendations based on the member’s responses and interviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommendations are intended to help create a more sustainable business; the Audit informs eligibility for funding and next-step programming.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding eligibility based on Audit results (up to $20,000)
rubrics_metrics.description: Members are eligible for as much as $20,000 in funding when they fulfill specific criteria based on the results of their Sustainability Audit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The John S. and James L. Knight Foundation funds the audits and associated costs; Google News Initiative provided additional stipends in 2022–2024. Funding is contingent on meeting audit-based criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sustainability Lab — unblock revenue barriers
rubrics_metrics.description: An eight-week course where participants focus exclusively on how to remove obstacles to generating more revenue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Developed with the Google News Initiative, the Lab is designed to identify and solve specific revenue-blocking problems; it's a focused, cohort-based instructional intervention to increase revenue.

rubrics_metrics.name: News Founder Challenge — test startup viability
rubrics_metrics.description: A short program to help entrepreneurs determine if the news platform they want to launch is viable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Participants receive specific advice for six weeks and challenges to accomplish from the GNI Startups Playbook; one-on-one consulting is available afterward to guide members to other LION programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: GNI Startups Playbook — follow structured startup guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: The GNI Startups Playbook is a tutorial of six chapters and four starter guides covering core startup topics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Playbook is frequently used as a step in LION programming; members are encouraged to follow its chapters and starter guides as practical guidance for launching and operating startup newsrooms.

rubrics_metrics.name: News Entrepreneur Academy — ongoing education and resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Program for owners who have launched their news platforms offering comprehensive courses, brief lessons, and a resource library.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Academy supports growth-stage organizations with targeted lessons and tools to scale operations and revenue; it's positioned as the next phase after foundational programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flexible programming tailored to diverse publications
rubrics_metrics.description: All programming is built with flexibility for the unique nature of each publication; members 'choose their adventure' among programs and expert advice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because LION members vary widely in size, revenue model, and mission, programming emphasizes adaptable modules and one-on-one support rather than one-size-fits-all mandates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Work-life balance and burnout prevention as part of sustainability
rubrics_metrics.description: Understanding how to achieve work-life balance helps founders avoid burnout and is part of building a sustainable organization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical support (e.g., delegating fundraising and finance tasks) is highlighted as enabling founders to focus on strategy and avoid burnout; staff wellbeing is tied to long-term sustainability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use benchmarks for planning (median revenue and staff-size guidance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Median annual revenue for a LION member is $130,000, generally sufficient for a staff of two or three — use such benchmarks for planning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These benchmarks give context for budgeting and staffing expectations; founders can compare their metrics to member medians to assess viability and scaling plans.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider organizational form and funding model (for-profit vs. nonprofit)
rubrics_metrics.description: Member composition: 65% for-profit newsrooms and 35% nonprofits — organizational form affects funding and strategy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choice of for-profit vs. nonprofit status influences revenue strategies, eligibility for grants/stipends, and growth plans; LION programming supports both types.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognition/awards as markers of operational excellence
rubrics_metrics.description: Operational resilience and business-of-the-year awards are cited as recognition of strong operations and business health.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Awards (e.g., LION’s Operational Resilience General Excellence Award, Business of the Year tiers) function as external validation of successful operational and business practices and can be goals or benchmarks for member organizations.
